title: Product profile
description: Properties of a specific product that determine how it must be built. Derived with the product-profile skill, written to .ship/PROFILE.json. Enumerations are open: an unlisted value is a capability gap, not an error.

first_value_event.description: The single moment this product becomes worth having, as an observable event.

state_owners.description: Which system is authoritative. Prefer the class name — 'a local component', 'the device runtime', 'local persistent storage', 'an app server', 'an external service', 'a human workflow', 'a shared live session' — optionally with detail after it ('the device runtime (audio element)'). Routing normalises concrete nouns onto these classes, but the class name is what makes selection unambiguous. Two owners for one value means one is a cache — say which.

identity_model.description: The smallest boundary satisfying a named reason. Derived with identity-access-decision.

distribution.description: Public distribution is what earns a landing page and SEO. Anything else does not get one.

criticality.description: Reversible work passes at 'usually succeeds'. Irreversible work must succeed every trial.

core_capabilities.description: What the product must DO, never what it is about. 'audio playback', not 'music'. Each entry must map to existing code, a selected skill, or a file under .ship/gaps/.

gaps.description: Capabilities no available skill covers. Normal, and reportable. Each has a contract under .ship/gaps/.
